key_insight: A three-modality fusion model combining ultrasound images, clinical data, and text descriptions improves fine-grained separation of breast fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumors.
clinical_relevance: This could help reduce misclassification of borderline phyllodes tumors as fibroadenoma and support better preoperative decision-making.
method: Built the FAPT-M dataset with 910 pathology-confirmed patients and reviewed multimodal records.
Used DenseNet for image features, CLIP-inspired text encoding, and lightweight clinical encoding.
Added clinical-conditioned modulation, cross-modal Transformer fusion, and dual-path representation learning.
evidence_signal: Under patient-level five-fold cross-validation, the model achieved 77.64% accuracy, 73.38% F1-score, and 89.74% AUC, outperforming multiple baseline approaches.
watch_item: Performance is promising but still requires external validation and careful integration into clinical workflows before real-world use.
paper_title: Multimodal Fusion for Fine-Grained Classification of Breast Fibroadenoma and Phyllodes Tumors
